name: Kushano-Sasanian Kingdom
native: Kūšān šahr (Middle Persian, 'domain of the Kushans')

predecessors.name: Western Kushans
predecessors.text: the western half of the Kushan realm under Sasanian governors titled Kushanshah: Bactria, Sogdia and the Kabul valley

predecessors.name: Eastern Kushans
predecessors.text: the Peshawar valley (Gandhara), the 184 cells Cliopatria moves from the Eastern Kushans to the Indo-Sasanian shape in 260

successors.name: Kidarites
successors.text: the northern part: Bactria and Sogdia, the 1,437 of 1,438 cells of Cliopatria's Kidarite shape of 358 that lie inside the Indo-Sasanian shape of 357

successors.name: Sasanian Empire
successors.text: the southern part of the Indo-Sasanian shape: the Hindu Kush side, the Kabul valley and Gandhara (about 1,148 of 2,585 cells); the Kushan Empire page, paraphrased: Shapur II took large territories in…

ledger.x: 260: the Kushano-Sasanian kingdom, Kushanshahs of Sasanian blood ruling the old Kushan west from Balkh, is drawn as its own state.

260: Gandhara, the Peshawar valley, is drawn Kushano-Sasanian. under Shapur I (240-270) the Sasanians went 'further to the eastern parts of their empire in western Pakistan'; 'The farthest extent of the Kushano-Sasanians to the east appears to have been Gandhara', apparently not across the Indus.
260: the kingdom is a Sasanian vassal from the dossier's first year.
350: Shapur II turns on the Kushano-Sasanian south.
358: the south passes to Shapur II.
360: the Sasanian Kushanshahs lose the north to the Kidarites and the vassal kingdom ends.
360: the Kushano-Sasanian kingdom ends as a territorial state (page: 'This administration continued until 360-370', infobox 'Disestablished: c.

wars.name: Shapur I's campaigns against the Kushans
wars.outcome: Shapur 'annexed most of the land of the Kushans' and conquered Khwarezm in 242; in 262 he 'burned the Kushan cities of Begram and Taxila'.

wars.name: Rebellion of Hormizd I Kushanshah
wars.outcome: Hormizd I Kushanshah, whose coins use the title Kushanshahanshah, rebelled against Bahram II and failed (Kushano-Sasanian page); the Kushan Empire page says, in paraphrase, that he rebelled against the Sasanian Empire while keeping Kushan titles and coinage.

wars.name: Shapur II's wars with the Chionites and the Kushans
wars.outcome: Shapur II 'gained the upper hand against the Kushano-Sasanian Kingdom' around 350 and made a treaty of alliance with the Chionites and Gelani in 358; the Kidarites page puts the struggle at 353-358.

wars.name: Kidarite conquest of Bactria
wars.outcome: The Kidarites under Kidara 'replaced the Kushano-Sasanids' in Bactria; the kingdom ended c.

certainty.note: The frontiers of this Sasanian sub-kingdom are approximate throughout: the Hindu Kush and Indus side ('apparently did not cross the Indus') and the steppe to the north; no treaty line is recorded on the pages opened.
